A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cognitive-tools work. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, individual-tool ablations, prompting comparisons and an example execution trace.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds comparator results, a motivational-phrase ablation, tool-use analyses and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The four cognitive tools, code tool, orchestration procedure and tool prompts are retained. Algorithm 1 documents the existing pipeline; removing motivational phrases is an experimental ablation, not a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mathematical coverage: AIME2024, MATH500, AMC and the math subset of Smolbenchmark. The added experiments reuse these tasks.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Chain-of-Thought and code-only comparators for all four open-weight models across three benchmarks. Table 4 adds GPT-4.1 with cognitive prompting on AIME2024, beyond its earlier inclusion only in the Smolbenchmark comparison.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce motivational-phrase removal, an executed-code control with outputs returned to the model, and output-token cost measurement. The retained benchmark sizes, model sizes, pass@1 scoring, answer parsing and GPT-4.1 judging remain unchanged as documented; newly disclosed decoding settings do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix B tests dependence on motivational phrases, analyzes tool frequencies across datasets and model families, examines tool co-occurrence, and measures computational overhead. The earlier individual-tool ablation and worked execution trace are retained, with the trace moving to C.1.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports Welch's t-tests finding baseline-versus-best-tool differences significant at p < 0.05. Appendix B.2 adds Pearson correlations of tool use. The existing declarations of 16 repetitions, more than eight runs, and standard errors are retained; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Table 4 replaces GPT-4.1 baseline/tool scores of 26.7/43.3 with 32.0/53.0, retains o1-preview at 44.6, and adds cognitive prompting at 42.0. The PDFs do not explain these revised estimates. New comparator, ablation, tool-use and token-cost results substantially expand the evidence, while retained open-model scores stay unchanged. Section 5.1 also corrects the +26.7-point gain's attribution from backtracking to understand question.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The added pseudocode explains the existing procedure, and the mathematical examples are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 5.4 strengthen the GPT-4.1 comparison from approaching o1-preview to surpassing it. The central contribution remains eliciting reasoning through modular cognitive tools without additional training.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds interpretations connecting harder tasks with planning/checking, suggests a recall-and-backtracking recovery workflow, and acknowledges an accuracy-cost tradeoff. These qualify the retained modularity account; the existing limitations concerning mathematical tasks, manual tools and model-specific prompts remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses decoding settings, including Qwen temperature 0.7, top-p 0.8 and top-k 20, and Llama temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.9. Algorithm 1 adds orchestration pseudocode. These improve documentation without demonstrating implementation changes; the detailed tool prompts were already present.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning around cognitive architectures, cognitive prompting, modularity, agentic tools and reinforcement learning are retained. The added CoT experiments use an already cited method.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits grammar and clarifies method descriptions while preserving the main narrative and section order. It adds acknowledgments and appendix subsections, and moves the existing Evaluation appendix from B to C.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains comparator rows and colored highlighting, Table 4 gains a prompting row, and Tables 5-8 plus Algorithm 1 introduce substantial new displays. Figure 2 is relocated with its plotted content retained; Figure 1 and the prompt/trace presentation remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked CoT and code-only controls on its main benchmarks, leaving an important ambiguity about the source of its gains. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through Table 3, supported by the motivational-phrase ablation, explicit token-cost analysis and improved implementation documentation. Reporting weaknesses remain: the GPT-4.1 revisions are unexplained, and the new Qwen2.5-32B code-only average is 50.2 although its three scores average 52.6. These issues temper, but do not outweigh, the stronger empirical controls.
